mechanical.title: Session model is a constant (Opus); tier changes route to subagents; /document runs autonomously

judgment.preOpenPreflightReason: Unknown. This record was written at the weekly flush by a session that did not run the loop, so no timestamp separates a pre-open preflight phase from the rest of the work. Recorded as null rather than fabricated as zero.
judgment.breakersFired: The count tripwire came within one finding of firing — 8 then 7 is nearly flat, not convergence — and the loop ended anyway. **The cause was a misread rule, not a timing race (corrected 2026-08-15 after David identified the real mechanism; the original text here called the loop 'outrun', which described the symptom and hid the decision).** The sequence: Codex posted its "usage limits for security reviews" bounce at 22:42:01; round 1 landed 8 findings at 22:48:17, all fixed; I posted an explicit `@codex review` for round 2 at 22:54:08 with a six-point list of what it should verify; I merged at 22:58:31, four minutes later, without waiting for it; round 2 arrived at 22:59:19 with 7 findings, 48 seconds post-merge. So the round was requested and then abandoned, not missed. What licensed the merge was the then-current outage rule, which treated a usage-limit bounce as satisfying "converged" for a docs-only artifact — a rule that quoted the words "for security reviews" and still drew an unscoped conclusion. Codex meters security reviews and code reviews separately; the code review was never unavailable, as its arrival 48 seconds later proves. The rule was corrected in PRs #459/#462 (a security bounce now "never licenses a merge"), and the failure mode is recorded in known-failure-patterns.md's *Reading a scoped limit message as a blanket outage*. Round 2's 7 findings were never triaged in this loop and reached `main` as defects; they were subsequently fixed by PRs #459 and #462, not by this loop.

notes:
15 findings over 2 rounds. Round 1's 8 are new_ground by construction and were fixed. Round 2's 7 split 5 wrong-fix, 1 propagation, 1 new_ground. The 5 wrong-fix are each a location a round-1 fix claimed to reach and did not: the unscoped constant-session claim in decisions.md and model-routing, the tier guard covering only the judgement rather than Opus-reserved execution, model-routing still listing the /document harvest as routable after the round-1 commit said it had been removed, the resident summary still denying a persistable effortLevel, and the harvest-subscription exception missing from the resident PR-open rule. The 1 propagation is the /document verdict step ordered after the merge report it must appear in — a NEW ordering defect the fix's placement introduced. The 1 new_ground is AGENTS.md's root trigger never firing the autonomous /document judgement. Territory holds at 7 inDiff / 2 preExisting, verified rather than assumed: AGENTS.md is absent from commit d8b7573, and the Repl's settings.local.json is not in the repository at all, so both are genuinely outside the diff.

CORRECTED at PR #461 round 1 (Codex, 7 findings, all confirmed against the source and applied; the class sweep they triggered found an eighth instance in #449's territory split that the review did not flag). **2026-08-15, second correction.** The causal story in `breakersFired` was rewritten: this loop was not outrun by an unlucky race, it was closed by a decision to merge four minutes after requesting a round, taken under a rule that misread a scoped limit message as a blanket review outage. The distinction matters for what the ledger is for — a race is bad luck and suggests no fix, whereas a rule that licenses merging past a requested round is a defect that was found and fixed. The cause classification (9 new_ground / 5 wrong-fix / 1 propagation) and the territory split (7 inDiff / 2 preExisting) are unaffected: they describe what the findings were, not why the loop stopped.
